messages:
jen: FYI - I opened this thread to capture comp eligibility and comm plan after the EU inference region degradation earlier today. Root cause is on the infra side (KV cache eviction storm) and we restored steady-state at 12:42 UTC. Impact window ~ 09:21 - 12:42 UTC (3h21m).
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0315-EU: Severity 2 -> mitigated. Pages: @jen @mike. Postmortem: <link to doc>.
mike: thanks. do we have number of customers affected / metrics? need to know who to notify for credits.
jen: quick snapshot: ~120 tenants saw elevated 5xxs, peak error rate ~18% on requests routed to eu-1. Total tokens served dropped ~22% during window. I'll attach the raw query counts after this.
support-ops: pulling tenant list now. will flag any enterprise customers with active DA/commits.
jen: quick candidate list: 8 customers with reserved capacity (dedicated), 42 active hosted customers with >$1k/mo usage, remainder smaller.
lina-billing: ping on SLA rules — our contract language varies but standard hosted SLA is 99.9% monthly availability and credits pro-rated by outage minutes beyond SLA. For Dedicated it's handled under reserved capacity agreements; some have custom terms.
sam-csm: I'll triage customers who had open escalations earlier. we'll want a short customer-facing note and then a follow-up compensation offer if eligible.
alex-pm: do we have a recommended credit calc? ops wants a single consistent approach for hosted customers.
mike: simple math we usually use: allowed_downtime = 43.8 minutes/month for 99.9%. outage_minutes = 201 (3*60 +21). excess_minutes = max(0, outage_minutes - allowed_downtime). credit_pct = min(1.0, excess_minutes / (30*24*60)) * 100  -- but that's messy. propose we use a per-customer formula to compute dollar credit = monthly_commit * (excess_minutes / total_minutes_in_month).
lina-billing: agree with dollar-credit approach. sign-off: billing will calculate credits as: 
```
credit = round(monthly_commit_usd * (excess_minutes / (30*24*60)), 2)
```
We'll cap credits at 100% of monthly_commit. For customers without monthly_commit (pay-as-you-go), use last-30-day avg spend as base.
jen: okay. support-ops, can you produce a CSV with columns: tenant_id, tier(dedicated/hosted/payg), monthly_commit, avg_30d_spend, impacted_minutes? I'll attach the query.
support-ops: working on it, ETA 45m. pulling from billing and routing logs.
incident-bot: Deployment log: KV cache eviction threshold updated at 12:15 UTC, rollbacks applied at 12:38 UTC, final stable config at 12:42 UTC.
mike: while billing runs numbers, let's draft the customer comm. need short, empathetic, precise. here's a starting draft: 
```
Hi <CustomerName>,

We’re reaching out about an incident on 2026-03-15 that affected inference requests in our EU region between 09:21 and 12:42 UTC. During this time, you may have experienced increased errors and slower responses.

We deeply apologize for the disruption. Engineers have stabilized the service and we’ve deployed mitigations to prevent recurrence.

Next steps: we are assessing impact to your account and will follow up with any eligible service credits within 5 business days. If you had open support tickets related to this, your support rep will include specific details.

If you’d like a dedicated post-incident call, let us know and we’ll schedule it.

Sincerely,
The Redwood Inference Team
```

sam-csm: that reads well. suggest adding a line about immediate mitigation steps taken and a contact alias: incidents@redwood.ai. also include an opt-in for dedicated postmortem.
jen: added in final copy. mike, can you confirm SLA window wording is correct (we don't promise per-minute credits for Dedicated customers without custom clause)?
mike: correct — for Dedicated we'll follow the customer's contract; for hosted we'll use the standard 99.9% fallback. I'll add a billing note in the comms where applicable.
lina-billing: after we compute credits, we'll prepare individualized credit proposals in a CSV and a short template for invoices. ops: please mark tenants with reserved capacity so we can route to enterprise billing queue.
support-ops: CSV exported and uploaded to /shared/incidents/2045678901/impact.csv (link). includes impacted_minutes column and last_30d_spend.
jen: perfect. billing, please run the formula and post a sample for a mid-size hosted customer (monthly_commit=$5,000) so we can sanity-check.
lina-billing: sample compute: excess_minutes = 201 - 43.8 = 157.2 -> fraction_of_month = 157.2 / 43200 ~ 0.00364 -> credit = 5000 * 0.00364 = $18.2 -> round -> $18.20.
mike: small but correct; for larger customers with reserved capacity the credit could be larger since monthly_commit is higher.
sam-csm: let's prioritize customers with active escalations — we should call the top 10 before sending the mass email. I'll coordinate.
jen: ops/billing/support are we aligned on timelines?
support-ops: CSV done.
lina-billing: billing will finish calculations and produce per-tenant credit amounts in 2 business days.
sam-csm: I'll start outreach to top 10 today, target initial contact within 24 hours.
alex-pm: internal comm: can we get an internal one-pager for execs and sales? short blurb + number of affected customers + projected total credits. mj? (not in thread)
jen: I'll prepare a one-pager draft and post it here when ready.
mike: one operational ask: record the set of mitigations and long-term fix timeline in the postmortem. ops noted kernel-level change and cache policy tuning required.
jen: noted. final note for handoff: once billing posts the CSV with credits, support-ops will send the tailored customer emails using the template above and cc billing for transparency. We'll keep this thread as the coordination log. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
